data.title: Tech-Led Rally Lifts Hang Seng, But Biotech Shares Lag
data.description:
Hong Kong shares rallied on Friday, with the Hang Seng Index gaining 425.56 points or 1.79% to close at 24,211.35, supported by strong gains in technology stocks.

The Hang Seng TECH Index outperformed, rising 124.46 points or 3.06% to 4,197.84, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index added 137.29 points or 1.71% to 8,147.87.

The HKEX Tech 100 Index also advanced 129.41 points or 2.08% to 6,348.15. However, the Hang Seng Biotech Index slipped 7.17 points or 0.05% to 15,678.02.

Technology heavyweights led trading activity, with Tencent Holdings rising 3.26% to HK$424.80 on turnover of HK$8.61 billion. Alibaba Group gained 2.59% to HK$107.00, while Xiaomi surged 9.72% to HK$25.96.

AIA Group added 2.89% to HK$71.25, while WuXi Biologics fell 0.46% to HK$53.85.

Total turnover on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange’s Main Board reached HK$209.19 billion, while the Growth Enterprise Market recorded HK$74 million.

Among the session’s biggest gainers, Brightstar Technology jumped 61.11% to HK$0.58, followed by Shimao Group, which rose 41.18% to HK$0.096.

On the downside, TH Medical-B plunged 34.17% to HK$183.00, making it the session’s biggest decliner among the listed counters provided.

data.title: KOSPI Stays Below 7,000 As Investors Weigh Semiconductor Profit Outlook
data.description:
South Korea’s KOSPI remained below the 7,000 mark, closing at 6,625 on Friday, as concerns over foreign fund outflows, slowing market liquidity and the sustainability of semiconductor profits continued to weigh on sentiment despite record earnings prospects.

The index has struggled to break out of its trading range for nearly three months, contrasting with US markets, where the Nasdaq and S&P 500 have continued to reach record highs amid enthusiasm for artificial intelligence-related stocks.

According to South Korean broadcaster SBS, average monthly trading value on the KOSPI fell from nearly 50 trillion won in May to 21 trillion won in September.

Individual investors have also become more cautious following a sharp market decline in July, while foreign investors have continued to withdraw funds from South Korean equities.

Concerns over the semiconductor outlook have added to the pressure. Although Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have benefited from strong demand for memory chips used in AI infrastructure, investors remain uncertain about how long elevated profit margins can be sustained.

The expansion of production capacity from 2028 could ease supply shortages, while monthly price growth for conventional PC DRAM and NAND memory has recently slowed to single-digit rates.

Investors are now looking to Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix’s earnings announcements later this month for further guidance on memory demand and pricing.

Hyundai Motor Securities researcher Kim Jae-seung said investors would be more comfortable buying memory stocks if sales volume continued to grow without a decline in prices.

The planned November listing of US artificial intelligence company Anthropic is also drawing attention, with investors watching whether it will sustain enthusiasm for AI investments or divert capital away from South Korean equities.

data.title: Wall Street Rallies Ahead Of Bank Earnings, Inflation Data
data.description:
Wall Street ended higher on Friday, with all three major US stock indexes posting weekly gains as investors looked ahead to third-quarter corporate earnings and inflation data due next week for clues on the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.31 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, while the S&P 500 gained 46.15 points, or 0.59%, to 7,811.51. The Nasdaq Composite added 172.83 points, or 0.64%, to 27,366.17.

Investors are preparing for a busy earnings week, with major US banks including JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Bank of America and Morgan Stanley scheduled to report results.

Analysts expect S&P 500 companies to post aggregate year-on-year earnings growth of 30.6% for the July to September quarter, according to LSEG data, led by the energy and technology sectors.

Market sentiment remained sensitive to developments in the Iran conflict. Oil prices initially fell after US President Donald Trump said Washington would not attack Iran before the midterm elections and described negotiations with Tehran as productive. However, Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate futures both settled 0.4% higher.

Among individual stocks, Humana surged 11.6% after government data showed 95% of its Medicare Advantage members were enrolled in plans rated four stars or higher for 2027.

Apple fell 1.1% following a report that it had asked some suppliers to cut production of components for its iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, amid rising memory chip costs and concerns over consumer demand.

Telecommunications stocks also slumped after SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, raising competitive concerns for US wireless operators. T-Mobile US, AT&T and Verizon fell between 8.8% and 13.3%.

Despite Friday’s gains, consumer sentiment remained under pressure, with the University of Michigan reporting a deterioration in near-term expectations to an all-time low.

The small-cap Russell 2000 ended the week below its previous Friday close, diverging from the broader market’s gains.

data.title: Singapore Market Records S$2.58 Billion Turnover As STI Slips

In the real estate investment trust (REIT) segment, CapitaLand Ascendas REIT slipped one cent or 0.46% to S$2.19. CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust stood at S$2.24, Mapletree Logistics Trust at S$1.08 and Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust at S$1.19.

The STI tracks the performance of the 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange by market capitalisation.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Rises 0.47% As Budget 2027 Lifts Sentiment
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended higher on Friday, with the FBM KLCI gaining 0.47% as investors welcomed Budget 2027 and bargain hunting supported a rebound following the market’s recent sell-off.

The benchmark index rose 7.44 points to 1,608.45 from Thursday’s close of 1,601.01, after trading between 1,600.55 and 1,609.94 during the session.

Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Budget 2027 could provide fresh catalysts for domestic consumption, infrastructure and selected growth sectors.

He said the recent market correction had brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, although persistent foreign selling remained a headwind.

“While persistent foreign selling remains a key headwind, domestic institutional support and resilient economic fundamentals should help cushion the downside,” he told Bernama.

Thong added that oversold conditions had encouraged bargain hunting, supported by firmer regional emerging markets. However, elevated energy prices and bond market volatility continued to pose risks, with Brent crude easing 1.3% to US$102.91 per barrel.

YTL Power International contributed the most among selected index movers, rising 14 sen to RM5.70. 99 Speed Mart Retail and Press Metal Aluminium each gained 11 sen to RM3.23 and RM7.23 respectively. The three counters collectively added 5.45 points to the benchmark.

Among other heavyweights, Gamuda rose 14 sen to RM5.09, Hong Leong Bank gained 38 sen to RM21.48 and Sunway added nine sen to RM4.40. Petronas Gas fell 68 sen to RM17.12, while IOI Properties slipped three sen to RM3.35.

Market breadth was positive, with 627 gainers outpacing 450 decliners. Another 547 counters were unchanged, 1,204 remained untraded and 13 were suspended.

Total turnover fell to 3.33 billion shares worth RM2.90 billion from 3.51 billion shares valued at RM3.46 billion on Thursday.

The FBM Mid 70 Index advanced 146.04 points to 17,683.11, while the FBM Emas Index gained 69.07 points to 12,098.83. The FBM Top 100 Index rose 66.29 points to 11,871.40, the FBM Emas Shariah Index added 69.95 points to 12,129.78 and the FBM ACE Index climbed 59.79 points to 5,654.57.

Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index gained 46.37 points to 18,424.82, while the Industrial Products and Services Index rose 1.92 points to 180.75. The Plantation Index added 20.47 points to 8,890.26, while the Energy Index edged down 0.77 of a point to 838.57.

data.title: Markets In China Close Higher Led By Mixed Sectors
data.description:
Chinese stocks closed higher on Friday, with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index up 0.05 percent to 3,813.79 points.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed 0.17 percent higher at 12,641.86 points.

Turnover of stocks covered by the two indices totaled about 1.9 trillion yuan (approximately 282.19 billion U.S. dollars), up from 1.68 trillion yuan on the previous trading day.

Film and television, precious metals, cybersecurity, and brokerage sectors led the gains, while computing hardware, wind power equipment, semiconductor, and banking sectors saw the biggest declines.

The ChiNext Index, tracking China’s Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises, gained 0.22 percent to close at 3,043.33 points Friday.

The STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China’s sci-tech innovation board, closed 0.34 percent lower at 1,726.71 points.

data.title: Gold Gains More Than 1%, RHB Maintains Short Position
data.description:
Gold prices rebounded more than 1% on Friday as a softer US dollar and lower oil prices supported bullion, although RHB Research maintained its short position on COMEX gold amid a bearish technical outlook.

Spot gold rose 1.4% to US$4,190.57 per ounce as at 6.30am GMT, or 2.30pm Malaysian time, after hitting a two-month low on Wednesday. US gold futures for December delivery also gained 1.4% to US$4,215.30.

The weaker dollar made gold, which is priced in the greenback, more affordable for holders of other currencies. Lower oil prices also offered support as concerns over Middle Eastern supply eased following US President Donald Trump’s remarks that Washington would not attack Iran before November’s midterm elections.

However, uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s interest rate outlook continued to weigh on sentiment. St Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said further rate hikes would be needed to bring inflation back to the central bank’s 2% target. Higher interest rates tend to reduce gold’s appeal as a non-yielding asset.

In its technical outlook, RHB Research said selling pressure on COMEX gold had eased during Thursday’s session, with the metal closing at US$4,157 after trading between US$4,128.10 and US$4,170.70.

Despite the rebound, the research house said the Relative Strength Index remained below the 50% mark, indicating that the overall technical setup was still bearish.

RHB Research expects gold to test resistance at US$4,300 if the recovery continues, but sees downside towards US$4,000 and potentially US$3,800 if selling pressure resumes.

It advised traders to retain the short position initiated at US$4,284.80, with a stop-loss at US$4,400. The research house will maintain its negative trading bias until gold crosses above US$4,400.

Among other precious metals, spot silver rose 1.5% to US$60.22 per ounce, platinum gained 2.7% to US$1,677.80 while palladium climbed 3.3% to US$1,159.70.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Up Marginally At Midday As Investors Await Budget 2027
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its gains at midday on Oct 9, with the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rising 6.08 points as buying interest in selected heavyweight stocks lifted the market ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027.

At 12.30pm, the FBM KLCI gained 6.08 points, or 0.38%, to 1,607.09 from the previous day’s closing of 1,601.01, supported by consumer products and services, telecommunications and media, and industrial products and services counters.

The benchmark index traded between 1,600.55 and 1,609.94 during the morning session.

The broader indices also advance, with the FBM 70 climbing 114.79 points, or 0.65%, to 17,651.86, outperforming the benchmark index. The FBM Emas advanced 52.87 points, or 0.44%, to 12,082.63, while the FBM Shariah rose 65.50 points, or 0.54%, to 12,125.33. The F4GBM added 4.20 points, or 0.43%, to 978.39.

Market breadth was marginally positive too, with 478 gainers against 469 decliners, while 502 counters remained unchanged, 1,379 untraded and 13 suspended.

MI Technovation Bhd led the gainers, surging 62 sen to RM6.70, followed by United Plantations Bhd, which jumped 52 sen to RM30.92. Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd advanced 32 sen to RM43.82, while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd rose 18 sen to RM20.72. Nestlé (M) Bhd gained 16 sen to RM89.60.

On the losing end, Petronas Gas Bhd recorded the steepest decline, falling 38 sen to RM17.42, followed by Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd, which slipped 18 sen to RM20.46.

Genting Plantations Bhd shed 16 sen to RM5.58, Allianz Malaysia Bhd declined 12 sen to RM20.04, while FCW Holdings Bhd eased 11 sen to RM1.70.

Meanwhile, Zetrix AI Bhd emerged as the most actively traded counter, with 172.9 million shares changing hands as its share price rose half a sen to eight sen. Dagang NeXchange Bhd followed with 86.23 million shares traded, slipping half a sen to 52 sen, while Xidelang Holdings Ltd remained unchanged at half a sen on volume of 42.11 million shares.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd declined three sen to 84.5 sen, with 38.92 million shares traded, while VS Industry Bhd gained half a sen to 33.5 sen on turnover of 38.87 million shares.

Trading volume stood at 2.03 billion shares valued at RM1.34 billion.

Investors remained focused on the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at 3.30pm, with attention on fiscal measures, economic growth initiatives and sector-specific allocations.

data.title: Asian Stocks Slide As AI Spending Fears And Bond Yields Weigh
data.description:
Asian stocks fell on Friday and were heading for a second consecutive weekly loss as investors weighed concerns over heavy artificial intelligence investment, elevated bond yields and rising energy prices.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slipped 0.16%, putting it on track for a weekly decline of more than 1%. Japan’s Nikkei fell more than 1%, while markets in South Korea and Taiwan were closed for a holiday.

Brent crude futures traded at US$103.70 a barrel during Asian hours after surging more than 4% in the previous session, with the Middle East conflict fuelling inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates.

Although US President Donald Trump said Washington would not attack Iran before the November midterm elections, investors remained cautious over whether the conflict could escalate.

“The big question for markets is whether Trump sticks to his word if Iranian attacks intensify,” said Nick Twidale, chief market strategist at ATFX Global.

Technology shares led Wall Street lower overnight after a report that OpenAI’s annualised revenue was US$20 billion below what the company had previously indicated. The report added to concerns over the scale of investment required to sustain AI growth.

Investors are also watching a wave of potential fundraising by SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle to finance purchases of high-end AI chips. Meanwhile, Australian data centre operator Firmus shelved its planned US$5 billion initial public offering, citing market volatility and opting for private fundraising instead.

Higher energy costs, expectations of interest rate hikes and concerns over government debt have driven a prolonged global bond sell-off, pushing borrowing costs towards multi-decade highs.

“With long-term yields back around multi-decade highs, investors no longer have the luxury of valuing AI growth in a low-cost-of-capital world,” said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

In Europe, investors remained focused on France’s debt burden, budget deficit and political outlook ahead of its 2027 presidential election. The US 10-year Treasury yield was steady at 5.226%, while the euro traded at US$1.122, near a 17-month low.

Reuters

data.title: FBM KLCI Struggles To Rebound Ahead Of Budget 2027
data.description:
The FBM KLCI opened marginally higher on Friday as Apex Securities cautioned that elevated oil prices, persistent foreign selling and geopolitical uncertainty could limit a market recovery ahead of Budget 2027.

The benchmark index stood at 1,602.94 at the opening, with most heavyweight stocks struggling to rebound after recent losses.

Apex Securities said global equities faced continued pressure from rising long-term bond yields and signs of strain in the artificial intelligence trade, while oil prices remained sensitive to developments in the US-Iran conflict, per The Star.

“Though equities have been resilient, further upside in long-end yields could bring more significant headwinds, and a higher-for-longer rate environment looks set to persist,” the research house said.

Brent crude futures for December delivery rose above US$103 a barrel overnight after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement attacked Saudi Arabia, while a storm approached oil-producing areas in the Gulf of Mexico.

Apex expects the local market to remain volatile in the near term, with oil price movements, foreign fund flows and geopolitical developments likely to outweigh domestic catalysts before Budget 2027 is tabled on Friday.

“We stay cautious to conservative on the local bourse, as persistent foreign selling, elevated crude oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty are likely to cap any rebound,” it said, identifying the Budget as the next key event for market direction.

Among actively traded counters, Dnex gained half a sen to 53 sen, L&G rose half a sen to 19.5 sen, while XDL was unchanged at 0.5 sen.

data.title: Ringgit Opens Higher Ahead Of Budget 2027
data.description:
The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Friday as investors remained cautious ahead of Budget 2027, with the government’s fiscal outlook expected to be a key focus.

At 8am, the local currency rose to 4.0880/0945 against the US dollar from Thursday’s close of 4.0890/0940.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said markets would be watching whether the government maintained fiscal discipline and continued to reduce the fiscal deficit.

He said this would be particularly important given political considerations surrounding the Budget, with state elections approaching and a general election expected in the future.

“Maintaining fiscal discipline will remain a key factor in strengthening the ringgit, as it will ensure that economic fundamentals continue to support the Malaysian currency,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit weakened at the open, slipping to 4.5839/5912 against the euro from 4.5719/5775 at Thursday’s close. It also fell to 2.5862/5905 against the Japanese yen from 2.5834/5867 and declined to 5.4076/4162 against the British pound from 5.3930/3996.

The ringgit traded mixed against regional currencies, weakening to 3.1918/1971 against the Singapore dollar from 3.1893/1934 and strengthening against the Thai baht to 12.1468/1715 from 12.1371/1563.

It was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.51 and the Indonesian rupiah at 228.2/228.6.

data.title: HSIF Face Further Downside Towards 23,600, RHB
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) is maintaining its short position on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract fell for a second consecutive session on Thursday, with further downside towards 23,600 points in sight.

HSIF dropped 343 points to close at 23,773 points, having opened at 24,109 points and traded between an intraday high of 24,126 points and a low of 23,692 points. It recovered 29 points during the evening session to last trade at 23,802 points.

RHB Research said the latest candlestick formation, marked by a lower low and a lower high, indicated that bearish momentum remained intact. The research house expects the correction to potentially extend towards immediate support at 23,600 points, followed by the next support at 23,100 points.

The research house is sticking with the short position initiated at the close of Sept 17, when HSIF stood at 24,572 points, citing a persistently bearish technical setup. It has also revised the stop-loss level to 25,000 points to help manage trading risks.

Any rebound is expected to face selling pressure at 24,300 points, which remains the first resistance level. The revised stop-loss level of 25,000 points marks the next resistance.

RHB Research said traders should maintain a negative trading stance while the technical outlook remains bearish.

data.title: Wall Street Mixed As Crude Prices Surge And Chipmakers Slide
data.description:
US stocks ended mixed on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 1.25% as semiconductor shares slumped and a sharp rise in crude oil prices fuelled concerns over inflation and further interest rate hikes.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 51.77 points, or 0.10%, to 51,231.64. The S&P 500 fell 36.41 points, or 0.47%, to 7,765.36, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 345.35 points to close at 27,193.34.

Oil prices climbed after attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz heightened supply concerns, compounded by a reduction in US output due to hurricane activity. West Texas Intermediate crude settled 3.6% higher, while Brent crude gained 4.1%.

The rally has added to inflationary pressure, with US crude prices already up more than 60% this year amid the war involving Iran. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September for the first time since July 2023, and markets are pricing in a 69.2% probability of another increase in December, according to CME’s FedWatch tool. Rates are widely expected to remain unchanged this month.

Semiconductor stocks were among the biggest drags on the market, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 3.4%. The decline followed a Financial Times report that OpenAI’s annualised revenue was US$20 billion below what the company had previously indicated.

Micron Technology dropped 4.8%, while Broadcom and Oracle fell 4.4% and 5.5%, respectively. The latter two companies also faced pressure after the Wall Street Journal reported that Broadcom was arranging US$50 billion in financing for OpenAI, while Oracle was seeking an unspecified amount. The prospect of large technology-related debt issuance has raised concerns about competition for capital.

“The market’s going sideways in anticipation of third-quarter earnings season, which begins next week, and then there’s the ongoing conflict in Iran that’s pushing oil prices higher,” said Terry Sandven, chief equity strategist at US Bank Wealth Management in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

“What’s equally telling is that year-to-date, the path of least resistance for equities has been up.”

Technology stocks weighed on the S&P 500, while energy shares led gains among its 11 major sectors. Samsung Electronics’ forecast for record quarterly profit failed to lift sentiment, with its shares closing lower in South Korea.

Elsewhere, Palantir rose 2.4% after Goldman Sachs upgraded the data analytics software provider to ‘buy’ from ‘neutral’. PepsiCo gained 3.7% after announcing additional spending cuts alongside a lower annual core profit forecast.

Starbucks slipped 0.4% following reports that it was exploring a potential acquisition of Chipotle Mexican Grill. Chipotle shares jumped 6.2%.

Market breadth remained negative. Declining stocks outnumbered advancers by 1.28 to one on the New York Stock Exchange and by 1.33 to one on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded four new 52-week highs and 12 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite posted 33 new highs and 319 new lows.

Trading volume across US exchanges reached 18.81 billion shares, above the 20-session average of 17.74 billion shares.

data.title: Stock Picks: 99 Speed Mart And MTT Shipping & Logistics
data.description:

Meanwhile, MTT Shipping & Logistics could extend its upward movement after breaking above the RM1.15 resistance on strong trading volume.

A drop below the RM1.10 support level would signal a bearish breakout and raise the risk of further declines.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Reclassifies Xin Synergy Into Property Sector Effective Oct 12
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd has reclassified Xin Synergy Group Bhd from the Industrial Products and Services sector to the Property sector, with the change taking effect on Oct 12.

The stock exchange said the revised classification, effective from 9am, will also see Xin Synergy’s sub-sector changed from Building Materials to Property, reflecting developments in the company’s core business activities.

The company’s stock short name, XIN, and stock code, 7043, will remain unchanged.

Bursa Malaysia said the reclassification takes into account changes in the company’s business activities and the contribution of its core operations to its financial performance.

The move places Xin Synergy alongside other property-sector counters on Bursa Malaysia, giving investors an updated sector classification when assessing the company’s business profile.

Bursa Malaysia added that periodic sector and sub-sector classification updates are intended to keep investors and market participants informed of developments involving listed companies across the Main Market, ACE Market and LEAP Market.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Sheds 10.77 Points As Oil Price Surge, Budget 2027 Jitters Weigh On Sentiment
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its losses on Oct 8, with the benchmark FBM KLCI tumbling 10.77 points, or 0.67%, to 1,601.01 as investors remained cautious ahead of Oct 9’s Budget 2027 announcement, while surging oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia intensified selling pressure.

At the closing bell, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell from Oct 7’s 1,611.78, having traded between an intraday high of 1,613.45 and a low of 1,597.94.

The benchmark recovered slightly from its session low but remained firmly in negative territory, reflecting persistent risk aversion ahead of the much-anticipated national budget.

Losses extended across the broader market, with the FBM 70 Index suffering the steepest decline, plunging 216.42 points, or 1.22%, to 17,537.07.

The FBM Emas shed 95.19 points, or 0.79%, to 12,029.76, while the F4GBM slipped 8.13 points, or 0.83%, to 974.19.

The FBM Shariah declined 87.32 points, or 0.72%, to 12,059.83, underscoring the widespread weakness across the market.

The losses reflected heightened caution as investors assessed the potential impact of Budget 2027 alongside external uncertainties, particularly rising energy costs and geopolitical tensions.

Zetrix AI Bhd continues to dominate the most active list, with 237.25 million shares traded, slipping half a sen to 7.5 sen after moving between seven sen and 8.5 sen.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd followed with 112.64 million shares changing hands, gaining two sen to 87.5 sen, while VS Industry Bhd edged up half a sen to 33 sen on 106.02 million shares.

PUC Bhd remained unchanged at four sen, recording trading volume of 67.03 million shares, while JAKS Resources Bhd climbed one sen to 18.5 sen with 66.11 million shares traded.

Despite selective buying interest in several actively traded counters, the overall market remained weighed down by selling pressure.

Investors are expected to closely scrutinise Budget 2027 on Oct 9 for fiscal measures, development spending and sector-specific incentives that could influence market direction, while developments in West Asia and oil price movements remain key external risks.

data.title: Decliners Overwhelm Gainers As Selling Pressure Swept Across The Broader Market
data.description:
Selling pressure swept across Bursa Malaysia’s broader market, with decliners overwhelming gainers by more than two to one as investors continued to offload shares across technology, plantation and consumer-related counters.

Market breadth remained firmly negative, with 813 losers against just 378 gainers, while 482 counters were unchanged, 2,828 untraded and 13 suspended.

Trading activity also slowed, with total turnover easing to 3.51 billion shares worth RM3.46 billion compared to 3.83 billion shares valued at RM3.52 billion in the previous session.

The widespread weakness saw several heavyweight counters suffer sharp losses, although selective buying in energy and consumer stocks provided some support.

Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd topped the losers’ list, plunging RM1.70 to RM43.50, making it the biggest decliner in absolute price terms.

Plantation heavyweights also came under pressure, with United Plantations Bhd tumbling 78 sen to RM30.40 and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd shedding 56 sen to RM20.54.

UMS Integration Ltd declined 50 sen to RM8.80, while Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd dropped 46 sen to RM29.24, rounding out the five biggest losers.

The losses highlighted the extent of selling pressure across multiple sectors, particularly technology and plantation stocks.

Despite the broad-based sell-off, Petronas Gas Bhd emerged as the session’s biggest gainer, advancing 54 sen to RM17.80.

Nestlé (M) Bhd followed with a 42 sen increase to RM89.44, while Chin Teck Plantations Bhd gained 26 sen to RM10.54.

Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd also climbed 26 sen to RM3.77, with approximately 10.04 million shares changing hands, reflecting active buying interest.

Bus Cap Bhd rounded out the top five gainers, rising 18 sen to 99.5 sen on trading volume of about 11.03 million shares.

The contrasting performances underscored selective buying interest in a handful of counters, but gains were insufficient to offset the broader market weakness.

With declining stocks outnumbering advancing counters by a wide margin and overall trading activity moderating, the session reflected sustained selling pressure and cautious investor sentiment across Bursa Malaysia.
